$comment: The contract between the open-source CLI (oortmem/oort) and the Oort Cloud API (oortmem/oortcloud, apps/cloud). The CLI tests itself against a fake that follows this file; the API repo keeps an identical copy and tests the real Worker against it. Change both together.

routes.body: export format v1 JSON Lines, manifest first

hive.$comment: Constellations (CON-63): an invite-only beta behind accounts.hive_beta. Outside it every route here answers 403 hive_not_enabled. :c is a Constellation id or its name (URL-encoded); one the caller is not a member of answers 404, exactly like one that does not exist. Recall reads the caller's Constellations (at most 4) on its own; a hive memory carries origin.level 'hive' and origin.node 'Constellation <name>' ('Constellation <name> · contested' while it is held against another memory for a maintainer), and a dropped hive leg is listed in degradedNodes as { node, reason } with 'hive-unavailable' in degraded. A share is two calls: the preview (by id or name; a name several of yours share answers 409 ambiguous_constellation listing them with their ids) returns constellationId, and a previewToken; the confirm (confirm: true) must name that id in the path (a name is refused with 400 confirm_by_id), present the previewToken and exactly the previewed text (409 preview_required otherwise), and send acknowledgedFindings: true when the preview found personal data (409 findings_unacknowledged). A memory whose project's privacy no client has stated is refused with 409 project_privacy_unknown; observe, recall and share carry projectPrivate for the current project only when its config file sets it; a recorded true is never cleared by a later false, only by PUT /v1/projects/:project/privacy (the owner's explicit choice). A member may share 30 memories a day per Constellation and a Constellation holds at most 5,000 (429 share_limit); sharing the same memory again updates its one copy. Members (CON-64): joining is by invitation only. A maintainer invites an email address with a role (maintainer, member or reader); the invite is a single-use token, valid 7 days, stored only as a hash, shown to the inviter as a link (and emailed when the service can send mail). It is looked up and accepted only from the signed-in dashboard with the person's verified addresses: lookup names the Constellation and role (matches: true) only when one of them is the invited address, and otherwise only whom the invite is for (matches: false); accept refuses a mismatch (403 email_mismatch). Roles: a maintainer invites, removes, changes roles, binds projects and sets policy; a member recalls, shares and attaches their own agents; a reader recalls, and may attach agents that read only. The owner is a maintainer who cannot be removed or leave; only the owner transfers ownership or deletes the Constellation. A refusal for a role answers 403 role_required; a plan's member limit answers 403 plan_limit. :member is the id members lists (mb_…) or the member's invited email address. An attached agent (a Star) reads, and with share: true shares, a Constellation only within its owner's role; a recall or whoami that names an agent reads only the Constellations that agent is attached to, and one that names none reads all of the caller's. A narrowed key (POST /v1/keys with scope) or a connector reaches only the Constellations it was granted: others answer 404 as if they did not exist, and a right it lacks answers 403 scope_denied. Membership changes reach every vault within 60 seconds. Invites are limited: 10 pending per Constellation (429 invite_limit). Invite emails are limited per inviter and per address per day; past those the invite is still made and the link returned, with emailed: false and a note saying why. A narrowed key cannot change membership or maintain (invite, revoke, remove, role, leave, attach, detach, transfer, policy, projects, delete: 403 scope_denied). When an inviter stops being a maintainer their pending invites are revoked; one whose inviter lost the role since answers 410 invite_revoked. Disagreements (CON-66): a share is compared with the Constellation's current memories, and a confirmed share answers outcome: added, updated (the same memory shared again), reinforced (id is then the memory it confirmed: a confirmation is counted, never an author), refined, superseded or corrected (a new version; the earlier one ended and stays its author's), history (an older claim, stored already ended) or contested. Contest labels rest on the model's judgment of what contradicts what: advisory, not a guarantee against a member who words a claim to avoid it. Trust is maintainer > member > reader; a narrowed key or a connector carries member at most. supersedeTrust (member by default, or maintainer; set with the policy route, which takes policy, supersedeTrust or both) is the least trust a contradiction of someone else's memory needs: below it the share is stored as its own memory, both stay current, labelled contested, and GET /v1/constellations/:c/contested lists the pairs (current and challenger). A maintainer resolves one with POST /v1/constellations/:c/contested/:id and { keep }: keeping the challenger applies what it asked for (SUPERSEDE or CORRECT), keeping the current memory retracts the challenger (RETRACT); a narrowed key answers 403 scope_denied, a member 403 role_required, and no open contest holding both ids 404 not_found.

galaxies.$comment: Galaxies (CON-97): a Galaxy is a Clerk Organization, mirrored into Oort's database by the site's webhook; every route here reads that mirror and never calls Clerk. Hive beta only (403 hive_not_enabled outside it), and only for a full key or the signed-in dashboard: a narrowed key or a connector answers 403 scope_denied and whoami lists no galaxies for it. :g is a Galaxy id (g_…), its slug or its name (URL-encoded), among the caller's own Galaxies; one the caller is not in answers 404, exactly like one that does not exist, and a reference matching more than one Galaxy (by id, slug or name) answers 409 ambiguous_galaxy listing the candidates with their ids. role is admin (org:admin) or member (any other Organization role), and owner for the Organization's creator while they are an admin: rights follow the current role alone. Galaxies are created and people invited on https://oortcloud.dev/dashboard/galaxies, signed in. Being added in Clerk grants nothing until the person accepts there (a "Join" click, signed in; never a key or a connector): until then the Galaxy is not listed for them, its admin rule does not apply to them, and its admins see them in members with pending: true. A re-add after a removal needs a new acceptance. An admin creates Constellations in it (POST /v1/constellations with galaxy, which must be the Galaxy's id: a slug or name answers 400 galaxy_by_id naming the id, so clients resolve it first; anyone else answers 403 role_required) and is at least a maintainer of every Constellation in it (demoting or removing them there answers 409 galaxy_admin); a member gets no Constellation access by being in the Galaxy and is invited as before. A Constellation made in a Galaxy belongs to the team: when its owner is removed from the Organization or stops being an admin, it moves to the Galaxy's owner (when an accepted admin) or else its longest-standing accepted admin; with none, it stays orphaned and maintaining it answers 409 orphaned until an admin accepts. Its ownership is transferred only to an accepted admin (409 galaxy_admin_required). Removing someone from the Organization, demoting them, or deleting the Organization ends what their Galaxy role gave them, and removal or deletion removes them from its Constellations, within 60 seconds; a deleted Organization's Constellations stay with their owners. whoami lists galaxies (id, name, slug, role) when the account has any.

archive.$comment: Deleted organizations (CON-102). When a Galaxy's Organization is deleted, its Constellations are archived: read-only for 30 days, then deleted. Their members keep reading them (GET /v1/constellations/:c, memories, recall, labelled 'Constellation <name> · archived') and export them (GET /v1/constellations/:c/export, JSON Lines, one memory per line); a share, an invite or a maintainer's change answers 409 constellation_archived; lists and GET /v1/constellations/:c carry archivedUntil (when it is deleted). Within the 30 days its owner may adopt it into their own account (POST /v1/constellations/:c/adopt, a full key or the dashboard; it needs their own Oort Pro): it is then theirs, outside any Galaxy, and writable again. Adopt answers 403 role_required for anyone but the owner, 403 plan_limit past the owned-Constellation limit, 409 orphaned for an orphaned one, 409 not_archived when there is nothing to adopt, and 410 archive_expired after the 30 days.

keys.$comment: API keys (CON-64). A key carries everything its account may do unless it was narrowed when it was made. scope lists 'planet' (always required: a key always reads and writes its own Planet) and Constellations by id or name, each optionally ':read' (recall only) or ':share' (recall and share); a bare Constellation carries every right the account's role has there. Only a full key or the signed-in dashboard makes keys (403 scope_denied for a narrowed key); a key made by a key is revoked with it. The response's scope is canonical (ids, not names), or null for a full key; the key itself is shown once and never stored.
